title: Proactive Latency Lens and Oncall Priority Optimizer
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a lightweight, SLO-aware ‘Latency Lens’ that fuses traces, metrics, and logs to surface caller-intent and error-mode signals, and use those signals to drive an Oncall Priority Optimizer. The optimizer produces per-incident paging priorities (P0/P1/P2) based on burn-rate context, affected customer tiers, and inferred request intent to reduce noisy paging and accelerate response for high-business-impact regressions.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Latency Lens dashboard shows fused top-10 latency signatures per service with trace links; 2) Priority Optimizer assigns and persists pager priority for real incidents in staging and matches manual reviewer decisions >= 85% of time; 3) Burn-rate alert rules can be scoped by inferred caller-intent and reduce false-positive pages in canary tests by >= 40%; 4) All schema changes are backward-compatible and documented; 5) End-to-end tests for synthetic probe + lens pipeline run in CI and pass.
out_of_scope: Full rewrite of tracing ingestion backend, instrumentation changes across >100 services. Deep ML model training for anomaly attribution beyond lightweight classification.
implementation_notes:
- Add a tracing-hook enrichment step that tags spans with caller-intent (API, batch, admin) using header heuristics and a small ruleset.
- Extend metrics pipeline to emit fused latency_signatures and error_mode counters derived from spans+logs.
- Implement an optimizer service that consumes fused signals, active burn-rate windows, subscription tier metadata, and outputs a priority score and recommended paging action.
- Expose a Latency Lens view in Console with linkable trace samples, signature diffing, and a recommended triage checklist.
- Provide a lightweight override API for SRE to tune priority mapping and set quiet-hours exceptions.
schema_changes: New metric: rl.fused_latency_signature (labelled: service, signature_id, intent, error_mode, sample_ts). New trace span tag: rl.intent and rl.error_mode. New alert label: rl_priority. All new keys are optional to avoid breaking older agents.
data_migration_plan: No historical rewrite. Start emitting rl.* metrics and span tags in staging for 2 weeks while running in shadow mode. After validation, flip production emitter and enable optimizer in read-only for 48h, then enable actioning.
rollout_plan: 1) Canary instrumentation to 10% of services (staging) for 2 weeks. 2) Enable Latency Lens UIs to internal users. 3) Run A/B test on paging: optimizer recommend-only vs optimizer actioning for 2 weeks. 4) Full enablement with monitoring and rollback playbook.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for enrichment rules and optimizer scoring.
- Integration tests: ingest sample traces -> fused metric generation -> optimizer output.
- E2E canary: validate reduced noisy pages and correct P0 escalation in simulated burn-rate events.
- Chaos test: simulate high-cardinality error bursts to ensure rate-limited paging behavior.
observability_and_alerting: Add internal SLI: rl.priority_mismatch_rate (percent of incidents where optimizer priority != reviewer priority). Add dashboard panels for optimizer decisions, signature churn, and per-tenant burn-rate impact. Create burn-rate variant rule: burn-rate scoped by rl.intent with lower sensitivity for admin/batch intent.
runbook_notes: Include decision tree: if optimizer assigns P0 and affected_customers=enterprise -> immediate page; if optimizer P1 but burn-rate>5x baseline -> page with single engineer; if rl.priority_mismatch_rate > 20% -> disable auto-action and open postmortem ticket.
security_considerations: Ensure rl.* trace tags do not contain PII. Enrichment rules must strip user identifiers. Access control: optimizer output only visible to SRE/observability roles until GA.
